name: Joseph R Janney

reading: He and his wife Josephine conveying land in 1900, land that had come to him by an earlier deed from a [?]Thirst and others. Confirms the wife named on his stone.

name: John Franklin Laycock
snippet: …of the one part and John F Laycock of the other … / …grant unto the said John F Laycock the … / …adjoining the lands of John F Laycock Landon … / …note then the said John F Laycock, under shall as…
reading: BEST SPATIAL FINDING OF THE SWEEP. He is the grantee - he bought this land - and a boundary is described as ADJOINING THE LANDS OF JOHN F LAYCOCK and a Landon. Landon Jones (b. 15 Dec 1819, d. 23 Feb 1902) is buried at Lakeview, so this places two people in the dataset next to one another on the ground. With Yardley Taylor's map this is how you locate a farm.

name: John Mahlon Chamblin
snippet: …eighty three between John M Chamblin trustee … / …convey unto the said John M Chamblin in trust … / …land, and the said John M. Chamblin [Cromants] … / …and seals [Michan] C Chamblin (seal) John M Chamblin (seal) …
reading: He acted as TRUSTEE on a deed of trust in 1883 - land conveyed to him to hold as security. A position of local standing, and a long way from the young man of 1860 living in his wife's parents' house.

name: George Franklin Everhart

reading: A transaction of sixty-four dollars, executed under seal alongside a Wm W Thompson. Note this is NOT the William W. Everheart who headed the 1860 household.

name: William Henry Beans
snippet: …E. P. Myers, William H. Beans, James Adams … / …Nelson Settle, A. T. Beans, and William H Beans, … / …[Settle], A. T. Bean William H. Beans, who being …
reading: A list of men named together and 'who being' - the formula for a jury or witnesses being sworn. He appears with A. T. Beans, a relative, plus E. P. Myers, James Adams and Nelson Settle. County court business spanning the war years.

name: A. T. Beans
snippet: …paid Dr Gallaher Self A. T. Beans " Board of …
reading: A GUARDIANSHIP ACCOUNT - payments for a doctor and for board. Guardianship records cover minors, which after a war means orphans; a record type not previously on this project's list and worth a sweep of its own.

name: Moses Daniel Wilson II
snippet: …of the one part and Moses D. Wilson of Fauquier … / …hand paid by the said Moses D. Wilson at or … / …unto the said Moses D. Wilson his heirs and …
reading: CAUTION - a Moses D. Wilson OF FAUQUIER buying land in FREDERICK county in 1837-38. Our man would have been 27 then, so the age fits, but the counties do not. Either he moved to Loudoun later or this is a different man of the same name. A reminder that the name is not unique, which bears on the unresolved father-or-son question.

name: Hamilton Station / the railroad
snippet: …of Alexandria to Hamilton Station, a distance of … / …'s Railroad from Hamilton Station Westward, in …
reading: The railroad line reckoned FROM ALEXANDRIA TO HAMILTON STATION as a known distance, with construction continuing WESTWARD from Hamilton. Recorded in a deed book of 1868-1871, so the line had reached Hamilton by then and the village was the railhead.

name: Hamilton Station in Loudoun records
record_set: Loudoun Deed Books 6-B and 6-D; Order Minute Books 21 and 22
reading: Every Loudoun record set mentioning 'Hamilton Station' falls in 1870-1875. The phrase does NOT appear in Deed Book 5-T (1860-61). See the retraction note in transcripts/saunders_1861_deed.txt.

name: John W Saunders - caution
snippet: …year 1879 . between John W. Saunders of the … / …Whereas the said John W. Saunders is engaged in… / …to enable the said John W. Saunders to cultivate …
reading: A crop-lien agreement by a John W. Saunders of SOUTHAMPTON county, not ours. The top-ranked John W. Saunders in Virginia full text is a different man; the name is not distinctive enough to follow on its own.
